description:
## Question

The verdict's go/no-go rule requires no open safety gap in the runtime contract (memory safety, cleanup on process death, hot code upgrade); performance gaps are acceptable. Classify the open runtime issues (e.g. stats across reloads defk-9qv, frame layout tags defk-ls8, hang-proof resume tests defk-juw, code-size blowup defk-6ag) and any untested promise as safety gap (required for done) or nice to have, and say what evidence closes each safety gap.

comments.text:
Resolution:
- Safety gap = any way that code which compiles, called with any arguments, can crash the VM, corrupt memory, leak memory permanently, or break cleanup on process death or hot upgrade. Not safety: performance, observability, devex, compile-time cost.
- The four ticketed issues are nice to have, not required for done: defk-9qv (__defk_stats__ across reloads: observability; document per-library meaning), defk-ls8 (frame layout tag: the per-library frame type invariant holds and upgrade_test.exs covers it), defk-juw (hang-proof resume tests: the bug still shows, as a hang), defk-6ag (code-size blowup: compile-time cost; becomes a limit with a clear error).
- New safety gap found: alloc/2 computes n * sizeof(T) unchecked; alloc(f64, 2^61) wraps to 0 bytes with length 2^61 and an out-of-range write crashed the VM (SIGBUS, exit 138). Required for done. Bug: defk-gtv "alloc/2 size overflow crashes the VM" (P1), including an audit of every size calculation.
- Reviewed safe by reading the code (to be tested): inputs are re-bound from the rescheduled argv on every resume, so moved heap binaries and GC are fine; the error path frees every owned buffer; process kill frees the frame (already tested).
- Evidence for "no open safety gap": (a) a runtime threat list next to the runtime-contract table in the verdict, each entry a test: defk-5fc "Runtime threat list with a test per entry"; (b) the differential tests of "How are kernels checked against Elixir mode?" also run once with kernels built under AddressSanitizer/UBSan, with generators including huge and negative sizes.

title: Which open runtime issues are safety gaps?
